lyrics:
[Intro: rain on a window, soft piano, a voicemail beep]

[Chorus: soft female voice, sung]
The line's still open, I never changed the number
Same old ring in the same old hall
The kettle's on and the porch light's burning
Whenever you're ready to call

[Verse 1: male rap, older voice, steady]
Hey, it's your dad. It's the first of the year.
I know you said don't call. I know. I hear.
I was hard on you, harder than my father was on me
Thought that was love. That's the only kind I'd seen.
Your mother says you're working, got a place across the bay
I drove past once. I didn't stay.
I'm not asking you to say it's fine
I'm just leaving this here. Take your time.

[Chorus: soft female voice, sung]
The line's still open, I never changed the number
Same old ring in the same old hall
The kettle's on and the porch light's burning
Whenever you're ready to call

[Verse 2: same voice, a year on, slower]
Me again. It's been a while. I counted. It's been two.
I quit the drinking. March. I thought I'd tell you.
Found your baseball glove out in the shed
Oiled it. Don't know why. Put it on your bed.
I go to meetings Thursdays, say the things I did out loud
Man, you'd laugh. Or you wouldn't. Either way, you'd be proud?
No. Scratch that. That's not mine to say.
I'm just leaving this here. It's okay.

[Verse 3: son's voice, younger, hesitant]
Dad. It's me. Don't pick up. Let it record.
I got all of them. I played them in the car.
I've got a boy now. He's got your stupid chin.
I yelled at him last week and I heard you coming in.
So I stopped. I knelt down. I said sorry to a kid.
That's the thing you never did. And then you did.
We're coming Sunday. He likes trains. He's four.
Don't clean up. Just be home. Leave the light on by the door.

[Final Chorus: female voice, strings, both men humming]
The line's still open, I never changed the number
Same old ring in the same old hall
The kettle's on and the porch light's burning
Whenever you're ready to call

[Outro: rain easing, a phone picked up mid-ring]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 80 BPM, 4/4, B minor. Slow, heavy and intimate, like talking in a parked car.

VOICE: Two rappers. The father: an older man, gravelly, plain and unhurried, more spoken than rhymed, softer in his second verse. The son: younger, tighter, hesitant. The hook is a woman's soft, breathy, folk-like voice, close and sad. No shouting.

INSTRUMENTS: A minor-key piano figure, a deep, slow kick and a dry snare, a warm bass guitar, a small string section entering at verse 3, rain and room sounds, a voicemail beep before each verse.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, rain and piano. 0:14 Chorus 1. 0:38 Verse 1. 1:26 Chorus 2. 1:50 Verse 2. 2:38 Verse 3, the son, strings in. 3:26 Final chorus. 3:52 Outro, a phone picked up at 4:14.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Turn-of-the-century storytelling rap: dry, close vocals, soft boom-bap drums, a lot of room sound.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: 'That's the thing you never did. And then you did.' at 3:10.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The original is a young star hearing too late from a fan. This is told from the other end of life, by a father, and it lets the answer come in time.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Stiff apology, humility, a held breath, reconciliation.
